verses.sloka: ततस्तां रजनीं व्युष्य भरत: सपरिच्छद: ।कृतातिथ्यो भरद्वाजं कामादभिजगाम ऺह ॥ २.९२.१॥
verses.transliteration: tatastāṁ rajanīṁ vyuṣya bharata: saparicchada: ।kṛtātithyo bharadvājaṁ kāmādabhijagāma ऺha ॥ 2.92.1॥

translations.english: Bharata with his retinue received the hospitality and spent the night at Bharadwaja's ashram. Then he approached Bharadwaja on his own.
translations.hindi: अयोध्याकांड का अड्टासीवाँ सग समाप्त हुआ ॥ १ स्वयंनतुमंत्रिमुखेन | (रा०) २ नाभिपत्स्यते-नाङ्गीकरिष्यति | . (गो०) ३ श्रनुवत्स्यामि - तद्नुचरो .भवामि। (गो०) र एकोननवतितमः संगः १्ठयुँष्य रात्रिंर तु तत्रेवर गङ्गाकूले स राघवः । भरतः ४काल्यपुत्थाय शत्रुघ्नमिदमब्रतरीत्‌

verses.sloka: तमृषि: पुरुषव्याघ्रं प्राञ्जलिं प्रेक्ष्य चागतम् ।हुताग्निहोत्रो भरतं भरद्वाजो ऽभ्यभाषत ॥ २.९२.२॥
verses.transliteration: tamṛṣi: puruṣavyāghraṁ prāñjaliṁ prekṣya cāgatam ।hutāgnihotro bharataṁ bharadvājo 'bhyabhāṣata ॥ 2.92.2॥

translations.english: Seeing Bharata, the best among men, who stood with folded palms, sage Bharadwaja, who had just completed his firesacrifice, said to him:
translations.hindi: शत्र न्न उठो ! सबेरा हो चुका । अब क्यों पड़े सो रहे हो । तुम्हारा कल्याण हो । तुम जाकर तुरन्त निषादराज गुद को यहाँ बुला लाओ, जिसमे वह हमारी सेना को पार उतारे

verses.sloka: कच्चिदत्र सुखा रात्रिस्तवास्मद्विषये गता ।समग्रस्ते जन: कच्चिदातिथ्ये शंस मे ऽनघ ॥ २.९२.३॥
verses.transliteration: kaccidatra sukhā rātristavāsmadviṣaye gatā ।samagraste jana: kaccidātithye śaṁsa me 'nagha ॥ 2.92.3॥

translations.english: O sinless one hope, you spent the night at our hermitage well? Tell me whether all your people enjoyed the hospitality?
translations.hindi: यह सुन शत्रू ने भी कहा-हे भ्राता | सञै-सो नहीं रहा-- लाग रहा हुँ और जिस प्रकार आप राम का चिन्तन करतेहें, वैसे ही मैं भी उन्हीं का चिन्तन कर रहा हू

verses.sloka: तमुवाचाञ्जलिं कृत्वा भरतो ऽभिप्रणम्य च ।आश्रमादभिनिष्क्रान्तमृषिमुत्तमतेजसम् ॥ २.९२.४॥
verses.transliteration: tamuvācāñjaliṁ kṛtvā bharato 'bhipraṇamya ca ।āśramādabhiniṣkrāntamṛṣimuttamatejasam ॥ 2.92.4॥

translations.english: Bharata saluted with folded palms the sage of great powers. And emerging from the hermitage, replied:
translations.hindi: व्युष्य--उषित्बा । ( गो० ) "ण्या क्या (गो?) राजि--रातो । (गो?) ३ परत यत्ररामो5शयिष्टतत्रैव । ( गो» ) ४ काल्यं--प्रत्यूष: - (गो०) बा० रा०--५५ इस प्रकार दोनों पुरुषसिंह बातचीत कर रहे थे कि इतने में निषादराज गुह!ठीक समय पर पहुँच और हाथ जोड़ कर भरत जी से बोला

verses.sloka: सुखोषितो ऽस्मि भगवन् समग्रबलवाहन: ।तर्पित: सर्वकामैश्च सामात्यो बलवत्त्वया ॥ २.९२.५॥
verses.transliteration: sukhoṣito 'smi bhagavan samagrabalavāhana: ।tarpita: sarvakāmaiśca sāmātyo balavattvayā ॥ 2.92.5॥

translations.english: O holy one, I with my ministers and the entire army of men and animals passed the night happily. All our desires have been gratified by you.
translations.hindi: हे काकुस्थ ! आप नदी के तट पर रात को सुखपूबक तो रहे। आपको या आपकी सेना में से किसी को किसी प्रकार का क्लेश तो नहीं हुआ

verses.sloka: अपेतक्लमसन्तापा: सुभिक्षा: सुप्रतिश्रया: ।अपि प्रेष्यानुपादाय सर्वे स्म सुसुखोषिता: ॥ २.९२.६॥
verses.transliteration: apetaklamasantāpā: subhikṣā: supratiśrayā: ।api preṣyānupādāya sarve sma susukhoṣitā: ॥ 2.92.6॥

translations.english: All of us including the messengers were released from fatigue and heat. We were wellfed and wellhoused and the night was wellspent.
translations.hindi: गुह के ऐसे स्नेह-सने वचन सुन, भरत जी ने भी श्रौरास के भक्त गह से यह कहा

verses.sloka: आमन्त्रये ऽहं भगवन् कामं त्वामृषिसत्तम ।समीपं प्रस्थितं भ्रातुर्मैत्रेणेक्षस्व चक्षुषा ॥ २.९२.७॥
verses.transliteration: āmantraye 'haṁ bhagavan kāmaṁ tvāmṛṣisattama ।samīpaṁ prasthitaṁ bhrāturmaitreṇekṣasva cakṣuṣā ॥ 2.92.7॥

translations.english: O venerable one O excellent of the ascetics I seek your leave. As I am proceeding to see my brother, bless me with a kindly look.

verses.sloka: आश्रमं तस्य धर्मज्ञ धार्मिकस्य महात्मन: ।आचक्ष्व कतमो मार्ग: कियानिति च शंस मे ॥ २.९२.८॥
verses.transliteration: āśramaṁ tasya dharmajña dhārmikasya mahātmana: ।ācakṣva katamo mārga: kiyāniti ca śaṁsa me ॥ 2.92.8॥

translations.english: O knower of righteousness Tell me which path leads to the hermitage of that righteous and magnanimous one (Rama)? And how far is it (from here)?
translations.hindi: रामस्यश्रनुबशः--रामस्यश्चतुचरः । ( शि. ) २ दाशा;-- कैवतंकाः ( शि० ) . एकोननवतितमः सग ८६७ भरत जी की ऐसी आज्ञा पा कर गुह ने बड़ी शीघ्रता से पुन अपने नगर में प्रवेश क्रिआ और वहाँ जा कर, अपनी जाति बालों ( मल्‍्लाहों ) से कहा-

verses.sloka: इति पृष्टस्तु भरतं भ्रातृदर्शनलालसम् ।प्रत्युवाच महातेजा भरद्वाजो महातपा: ॥ २.९२.९॥
verses.transliteration: iti pṛṣṭastu bharataṁ bhrātṛdarśanalālasam ।pratyuvāca mahātejā bharadvājo mahātapā: ॥ 2.92.9॥

translations.english: Thus questioned, the great sage, brilliant Bharadwaja replied to Bharata who was yearning to see his brother:

verses.sloka: भरतार्द्धतृतीयेषु योजनेष्वजने वने ।चित्रकूटो गिरिस्तत्र रम्यनिर्दरकानन: ॥ २.९२.१०॥
verses.transliteration: bharatārddhatṛtīyeṣu yojaneṣvajane vane ।citrakūṭo giristatra ramyanirdarakānana: ॥ 2.92.10॥

translations.english: O Bharata, three and a half yojanas from here in the lonely forest stands mount Chitrakuta, with its charming streams and woodlands
translations.hindi: गुह द्वारा ऐसा कहे जाने पर, मल्लाह लोग उठ खड़े हुए ओर अपने राजा के आज्ञानुसार उन लोगों ने इधर से जोड़ बटोर कर ५०० नावे ला कर, घाट पर लगा दी

verses.sloka: उत्तरं पार्श्वमासाद्य तस्य मन्दाकिनी नदी ।पुष्ऺिपतद्रुमसञ्छन्ना रम्यपुष्पितकानना ॥ २.९२.११॥
verses.transliteration: uttaraṁ pārśvamāsādya tasya mandākinī nadī ।puṣऺipatadrumasañchannā ramyapuṣpitakānanā ॥ 2.92.11॥

translations.english: On its northern side flows the river Mandakini which is densely covered with flowering trees and lovely blossoming woods (on its banks).
translations.hindi: इनके अतिरिक्त राजाओं के चढ़ने योग्य “स्वस्तिक” नामक एक बजरा नावे भी लाई गई । इन स्वस्तिक नावों में घंटे टंगे हुए थे पताकाएं शोभायमान थीं । हवा आने जाने क लिए बनी थीं, और नाव की तली में कीळे आदि ऐसी सावधानी - से जंडो थीं कि, उसमें एक बूँद -भी जल नाव के भीतर नहीं आ सकता था

verses.sloka: अनन्तरं तत्सरितश्चित्रकूटश्च पर्वत: ।तयो: पर्णकुटी तात तत्र तौ वसतो ध्रुवम् ॥ २.९२.१२॥
verses.transliteration: anantaraṁ tatsaritaścitrakūṭaśca parvata: ।tayo: parṇakuṭī tāta tatra tau vasato dhruvam ॥ 2.92.12॥

translations.english: O dear child, beyond that river lies mount Chitrakuta on which there is a hut made of leaves where, for sure, they both dwell.
translations.hindi: उन स्वस्तिक नाम के बजरों में सफेद ऊनी कालीन बिछे हुए थे। जब वे चलाई जाती थीं, तब उनमें छोटी छोटी घंटियाँ बजती थीं । वे देखने, में बड़ी सुन्दर जान पड़ती थीं। ऐसी एक नाव को गुह स्वय लाया था

verses.sloka: दक्षिणेनैव मार्गेण सव्यदक्षिणमेव वा ।गजवाजिरथाकीर्णां वाहिनीं वाहिनीपते ।वाहयस्व महाभाग ततो द्रक्ष्यसि राघवम् ॥ २.९२.१३॥
verses.transliteration: dakṣiṇenaiva mārgeṇa savyadakṣiṇameva vā ।gajavājirathākīrṇāṁ vāhinīṁ vāhinīpate ।vāhayasva mahābhāga tato drakṣyasi rāghavam ॥ 2.92.13॥

translations.english: O distinguished lord of the army, if you lead your army full of elephants, horses and chariots through the southern path or towards the southwest, you will come across Rama there.
translations.hindi: इस बजरे पर महायशस्वी भरत, शत्रुन्न, कौसल्या, सुमित्रा, तथा अन्य जो रानियाँ शीं, सवार हुई

verses.sloka: प्रयाणमिति तच्छ्रुत्वा राजराजस्य योषित: ।हित्वा यानानि यानार्हा ब्राह्मणं पर्य्यवारयन् ॥ २.९२.१४॥
verses.transliteration: prayāṇamiti tacchrutvā rājarājasya yoṣita: ।hitvā yānāni yānārhā brāhmaṇaṁ paryyavārayan ॥ 2.92.14॥

translations.english: When they heard about the journey, the wives of Dasaratha descended from their chariots worthy of them and stood around the brahmin, Bharadwaja.
translations.hindi: भरत आदि के नाव में बैठने के पूत्र पुरोहित तथा अन्य गुरुजन ब्राह्मण पहिले ही चढ़ चुके थे । तदनन्तर कौरशल्यादि रानियाँ नाव में बैठी थीं । उनके बेढने के बाद सामान से लदे छुकड़े नावां पर बोके गए थे

verses.sloka: वेपमाना कृशा ऺदीना सह देव्या सुमित्रया ।कौसल्या तत्र जग्राह कराभ्यां चरणौ मुने: ॥ २.९२.१५॥
verses.transliteration: vepamānā kṛśā ऺdīnā saha devyā sumitrayā ।kausalyā tatra jagrāha karābhyāṁ caraṇau mune: ॥ 2.92.15॥

translations.english: Among them was Kausalya, trembling, emaciated and desolate, along with Sumitra. They grasped the feet of sage Bharadwaja with their hands.
translations.hindi: सनन्दिघोषां--इषंजनककिङ्किणयादिघोषयुक्त । (गो०) २कल्याणीं-- शोभनां । (गो०) ३ ्रावास-सेनादिवेशं । (गो०) ४ आदीपयतां . अ्ग्निनांज्वलयतां । ( गो० ) ५ तीर्थ--श्रवतरणप्रदेशम्‌ । ( गो० ) ६ भाणडानि--उपकरणानि । (गो?) # पाठान्तरे--““मह्ाबलः” । जलते समय छावनी में जो घास फूस था, बह जला दिता गया । फिर गङ्गा जी में स्नान करने वालों का कोलाहल, तथा नाबों पर सामान लादने बालों का चीत्कार शब्द ऐसा हुआ कि, आकाश प्रतिध्वनित ही उठा। अर्थात्‌ वहाँ से सेना के कूच के ख्य ओर नावों में सामान लादते समय बड़ा होहल्ला हुआ

verses.sloka: असमृद्धेन कामेन सर्वलोकस्य गर्हिता ।कैकेयी तस्य जग्राह चरणौ सव्यपत्रपा ॥ २.९२.१६॥
verses.transliteration: asamṛddhena kāmena sarvalokasya garhitā ।kaikeyī tasya jagrāha caraṇau savyapatrapā ॥ 2.92.16॥

translations.english: Kaikeyi with her unfulfilled desire and despised in all the worlds overcome with shame, also grasped his feet.
translations.hindi: वे पालवाली नावे, जिन पर माँझी लोग बैठे हुए रखवाली छर रहे थे, नावों पर सवार लोगों को लिए हुए, बड़े वेग से चली जाती थीं

verses.sloka: तं प्रदक्षिणमागम्य भगवन्तं महामुनिम् ।अदूराद्भरतस्यैव तस्थौ दीनमनास्तदा ॥ २.९२.१७॥
verses.transliteration: taṁ pradakṣiṇamāgamya bhagavantaṁ mahāmunim ।adūrādbharatasyaiva tasthau dīnamanāstadā ॥ 2.92.17॥

translations.english: She reverently circumambulated that great and divine ascetic and stood not far away from Bharata with a sad heart.
translations.hindi: कितनी ही नावों में तो स्त्रियाँ ही खियाँ बैठी थीं ओर कितनी दवो नाबों में घोड़े ही घोड़े भरे थे। कई एक नावों पर रथ बैल छुकडे, घोडे, खच्चर”-जो बड़े बड़े मोल के थे भरे थे

verses.sloka: तत: पप्रच्छ भरतं भरद्वाजो दृढव्रत: ।विशेषं ज्ञातुमिच्छामि मातऽणां तव राघव ॥ २.९२.१८॥
verses.transliteration: tata: papraccha bharataṁ bharadvājo dṛḍhavrata: ।viśeṣaṁ jñātumicchāmi māta'ṇāṁ tava rāghava ॥ 2.92.18॥

translations.english: Then Bharadwaja, firm in his vows, said to Bharata, I want to know about your mothers individually.
translations.hindi: धीरे घीरे यें सब नावे गङ्गा के दूसरे पार पर जा लगीं और आरोदियों के उतारा । लौटते समय, गुह के बन्धु मल्लाह लोग, नौका ले जल में विविध प्रकार के खेल करते जाते थे

verses.sloka: एवमुक्तस्तु भरतो भरद्वाजेन धार्मिक: ।उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा वाक्यं वचनकोविद: ॥ २.९२.१९॥
verses.transliteration: evamuktastu bharato bharadvājena dhārmika: ।uvāca prāñjalirbhūtvā vākyaṁ vacanakovida: ॥ 2.92.19॥

translations.english: Thus asked by the sagacious Bharadwaja, Bharata, proficient in speech, replied with palms folded in reverence:

verses.sloka: यामिमां भगवन् दीनां शोकानशनकर्शिताम् ।पितुर्हि महिषीं देवीं देवतामिव पश्यसि ॥ २.९२.२०॥
verses.transliteration: yāmimāṁ bhagavan dīnāṁ śokānaśanakarśitām ।piturhi mahiṣīṁ devīṁ devatāmiva paśyasi ॥ 2.92.20॥

translations.english: O venerable sage, this queen you are looking at, forlorn and emaciated due to grief and fasting, and who resembles a goddess is Kausalya, the principal queen of my father. As Aditi bore Dhata, she bore Rama, the best among men who walks with the powerful stride of a lion.

verses.sloka: एषा तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम् ।कौसल्या सुषुवे रामं धातारमदितिर्यथा ॥ २.९२.२१॥
verses.transliteration: eṣā taṁ puruṣavyāghraṁ siṁhavikrāntagāminam ।kausalyā suṣuve rāmaṁ dhātāramaditiryathā ॥ 2.92.21॥

translations.english: O venerable sage, this queen you are looking at, forlorn and emaciated due to grief and fasting, and who resembles a goddess is Kausalya, the principal queen of my father. As Aditi bore Dhata, she bore Rama, the best among men who walks with the powerful stride of a lion.
translations.hindi: गुह के नोकर मल्लाह्रो ने स्वयं, गङ्गास्नान से पवित्र हुई सेना को पार उतार दिआ। बह सेना सूर्योदय से तीसरे मैत्र नामक मुहूत में परम मनोहर बन को।म्रस्थानित हुई

verses.sloka: अस्यावामभुजं श्लिष्टा यैषा तिष्ठति दुर्मना: ।कर्णिकारस्य शाखेव शीर्णपुष्पा वनान्तरे ॥ २.९२.२२॥
verses.transliteration: asyāvāmabhujaṁ śliṣṭā yaiṣā tiṣṭhati durmanā: ।karṇikārasya śākheva śīrṇapuṣpā vanāntare ॥ 2.92.22॥

translations.english: This lady plunged in grief, resembling the branch of a karnikara tree in the midst of the forest with blossoms withered and leaning on the left arm of Kausalya, is queen Sumitra, mother of two heroes, comparable to gods in beauty and possessing true prowess -- Lakshmana and Satrughna.
translations.hindi: प्रयाग में पहुँच, महामति भरत ने सब सेना तथा साथियों को मधुर वचनों से सान्त्वना प्रदान कर, जहाँ जिसको सुविधा थी उसे वहाँ टिकाया । तदनन्तर भरत जी, बसिष्ठादि ऋषियों को साथ ले, भरद्वाज जी के दर्शन करने को, उनके आश्रम की ओर प्रस्थानित हुए

verses.sloka: एतस्यास्तु सुतौ देव्या: कुमारौ देववर्णिनौ ।उभौ लक्ष्मणशत्रुघ्नौ वीरौ सत्यपराक्रमौ ॥ २.९२.२३॥
verses.transliteration: etasyāstu sutau devyā: kumārau devavarṇinau ।ubhau lakṣmaṇaśatrughnau vīrau satyaparākramau ॥ 2.92.23॥

translations.english: This lady plunged in grief, resembling the branch of a karnikara tree in the midst of the forest with blossoms withered and leaning on the left arm of Kausalya, is queen Sumitra, mother of two heroes, comparable to gods in beauty and possessing true prowess -- Lakshmana and Satrughna.

verses.sloka: यस्या: कृते नरव्याघ्रौ जीवनाशमितो गतौ ।राजपुत्रविहीनश्च स्वर्गं दशरथो गत: ॥ २.९२.२४॥
verses.transliteration: yasyā: kṛte naravyāghrau jīvanāśamito gatau ।rājaputravihīnaśca svargaṁ daśaratho gata: ॥ 2.92.24॥

translations.english: She is my mother Kaikeyi who is irascible, lacks the power of discrimination, proud, boastful of her beauty, ambitious of wealth, ignoble in the guise of a noble woman, wicked and intent on sinful acts. Behold her. You may know that because of her, Rama and Lakshmana the best of men entered the forest which may cause their destruction and king Dasaratha attained heaven. She alone is the root of this great calamity that I am presently confronting.

verses.sloka: क्रोधनामकृतप्रज्ञां दृप्तां सुभगमानिनीम् ।ऐश्वर्यकामां कैकेयीमनार्य्यामार्यरूपिणीम् ॥ २.९२.२५॥
verses.transliteration: krodhanāmakṛtaprajñāṁ dṛptāṁ subhagamāninīm ।aiśvaryakāmāṁ kaikeyīmanāryyāmāryarūpiṇīm ॥ 2.92.25॥

translations.english: She is my mother Kaikeyi who is irascible, lacks the power of discrimination, proud, boastful of her beauty, ambitious of wealth, ignoble in the guise of a noble woman, wicked and intent on sinful acts. Behold her. You may know that because of her, Rama and Lakshmana the best of men entered the forest which may cause their destruction and king Dasaratha attained heaven. She alone is the root of this great calamity that I am presently confronting.

verses.sloka: ममैतां मातरं विद्धि नृशंसां पापनिश्चयाम् ।यतो मूलं हि पश्यामि व्यसनं महदात्मन: ॥ २.९२.२६॥
verses.transliteration: mamaitāṁ mātaraṁ viddhi nṛśaṁsāṁ pāpaniścayām ।yato mūlaṁ hi paśyāmi vyasanaṁ mahadātmana: ॥ 2.92.26॥

translations.english: She is my mother Kaikeyi who is irascible, lacks the power of discrimination, proud, boastful of her beauty, ambitious of wealth, ignoble in the guise of a noble woman, wicked and intent on sinful acts. Behold her. You may know that because of her, Rama and Lakshmana the best of men entered the forest which may cause their destruction and king Dasaratha attained heaven. She alone is the root of this great calamity that I am presently confronting.

verses.sloka: इत्युक्त्वा नरशार्दूलो बाष्पगद्गदया गिरा ।स निशश्वास ताम्राक्षो नाग: क्रुद्ध इव श्वसन् ॥ २.९२.२७॥
verses.transliteration: ityuktvā naraśārdūlo bāṣpagadgadayā girā ।sa niśaśvāsa tāmrākṣo nāga: kruddha iva śvasan ॥ 2.92.27॥

translations.english: Thus spoke Bharata, the best of men, with his eyes reddened and voice choked with sobs and hissing like a king cobra.

verses.sloka: भरद्वाजो महर्षिस्तं ब्रुवन्तं भरतं तथा ।प्रत्युवाच महाबुद्धिरिदं वचनमर्थवत् ॥ २.९२.२८॥
verses.transliteration: bharadvājo maharṣistaṁ bruvantaṁ bharataṁ tathā ।pratyuvāca mahābuddhiridaṁ vacanamarthavat ॥ 2.92.28॥

translations.english: Hearing the words of Bharata, the great sage, wise Bharadwaja replied with meaningful words:

verses.sloka: न दोषेणावगन्तव्या कैकेयी भरत त्वया ।रामप्रव्राजनं ह्येतत् सुखोदर्कं भविष्यति ॥ २.९२.२९॥
verses.transliteration: na doṣeṇāvagantavyā kaikeyī bharata tvayā ।rāmapravrājanaṁ hyetat sukhodarkaṁ bhaviṣyati ॥ 2.92.29॥

translations.english: O Bharata, you should not find fault with Kaikeyi. Rama's banishment will prove a great source of happiness in future (for mankind).

verses.sloka: देवानां दानवानां च ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम् ।हितमेव भविष्यद्धि रामप्रव्राजनादिह ॥ २.९२.३०॥
verses.transliteration: devānāṁ dānavānāṁ ca ṛṣīṇāṁ bhāvitātmanām ।hitameva bhaviṣyaddhi rāmapravrājanādiha ॥ 2.92.30॥

translations.english: Banishment of Rama will bring about the welfare of the gods, the demons, and the sages of purified souls.

verses.sloka: अभिवाद्य तु संसिद्ध: कृत्वा चैनं प्रदक्षिणम् ।आमन्त्र्य भरत: सेन्यं युज्यतामित्यचोदयत् ॥ २.९२.३१॥
verses.transliteration: abhivādya tu saṁsiddha: kṛtvā cainaṁ pradakṣiṇam ।āmantrya bharata: senyaṁ yujyatāmityacodayat ॥ 2.92.31॥

translations.english: Having paid obeisance, the accomplished Bharata circumambulated sage Bharadwaja, look leave of him, and ordered his army to get ready.

verses.sloka: ततो वाजिरथान् युक्त्वा दिव्यान् हेमपरिष्कृतान् ।अध्यारोहत् प्रयाणार्थी बहून् बहुविधो जन: ॥ २.९२.३२॥
verses.transliteration: tato vājirathān yuktvā divyān hemapariṣkṛtān ।adhyārohat prayāṇārthī bahūn bahuvidho jana: ॥ 2.92.32॥

translations.english: Different groups of people intending to depart harnessed excellent horsechariots decorated with gold.

verses.sloka: गजकन्या गजाश्चैव हेमकक्ष्या: पताकिन: ।जीमूता इव घर्मान्ते सघोषा: सम्प्रतस्थिरे ॥ २.९२.३३॥
verses.transliteration: gajakanyā gajāścaiva hemakakṣyā: patākina: ।jīmūtā iva gharmānte saghoṣā: sampratasthire ॥ 2.92.33॥

translations.english: The male and female elephants wearing golden girths and decorated with pennants, set forth with their bells sounding like thunderclouds at the end of summer.

verses.sloka: विविधान्यपि यानानि महान्ति च लघूनि च ।प्रययु: सुमहार्हाणि पादैरेव पदातय: ॥ २.९२.३४॥
verses.transliteration: vividhānyapi yānāni mahānti ca laghūni ca ।prayayu: sumahārhāṇi pādaireva padātaya: ॥ 2.92.34॥

translations.english: Various types of costly carriages, large and small, set forth, while the infantry marched on.

verses.sloka: अथ यानप्रवेकैस्तु कौसल्याप्रमुखा: स्त्रिय: ।रामदर्शनकांक्षिण्य: प्रययुर्मुदितास्तदा ॥ २.९२.३५॥
verses.transliteration: atha yānapravekaistu kausalyāpramukhā: striya: ।rāmadarśanakāṁkṣiṇya: prayayurmuditāstadā ॥ 2.92.35॥

translations.english: The women headed by Kausalya, eager to see Rama, proceeded delightfully in distinguished carriages.

verses.sloka: चन्द्रार्कतरुणाभासां नियुक्तां शिबिकां शुभाम् ।आस्थाय प्रययौ श्रीमान् भरत: सपरिच्छद: ॥ २.९२.३६॥
verses.transliteration: candrārkataruṇābhāsāṁ niyuktāṁ śibikāṁ śubhām ।āsthāya prayayau śrīmān bharata: saparicchada: ॥ 2.92.36॥

translations.english: Magnanimous Bharata got into an auspicious palanquin of the splendour of the Sun and the Moon kept ready and proceeded amidst escorts.

verses.sloka: सा प्रयाता महासेना गजवाजिरथाकुला ।दक्षिणां दिशमावृत्य महामेघ इवोत्थित: ॥ २.९२.३७॥
verses.transliteration: sā prayātā mahāsenā gajavājirathākulā ।dakṣiṇāṁ diśamāvṛtya mahāmegha ivotthita: ॥ 2.92.37॥

translations.english: That vast army teeming with elephants, horses and chariots proceeded southward spreading like a lofty cloud that had risen in the sky, traversing through the forests full of birds and beasts, passing through the mountains and streams on the other side of the river Ganga.

verses.sloka: वनानि तु व्यतिक्रम्य जुष्टानि मृगपक्षिभि: ।गङ्गाया: परवेलायां गिरिष्वपि नदीषु च ॥ २.९२.३८॥
verses.transliteration: vanāni tu vyatikramya juṣṭāni mṛgapakṣibhi: ।gaṅgāyā: paravelāyāṁ giriṣvapi nadīṣu ca ॥ 2.92.38॥

translations.english: That vast army teeming with elephants, horses and chariots proceeded southward spreading like a lofty cloud that had risen in the sky, traversing through the forests full of birds and beasts, passing through the mountains and streams on the other side of the river Ganga.

verses.sloka: सा सम्प्रहृष्टद्विजवाजियोधा वित्रासयन्ती मृगपक्षिसङ्घान् ।महद्वनं तत्प्रतिगाहमाना रराज सेना भरतस्य तत्र ॥ २.९२.३९ ॥
verses.transliteration: sā samprahṛṣṭadvijavājiyodhā vitrāsayantī mṛgapakṣisaṅghān ।mahadvanaṁ tatpratigāhamānā rarāja senā bharatasya tatra ॥ 2.92.39 ॥

translations.english: Bharata's army of soldiers, elephants and horses, all in high spirits, looked splendid while entering the forest full of frightening flocks of birds and beasts. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे द्विनवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetysecond sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
